title: Little Feat - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in Los Angeles in 1969 by Lowell George, Roy Estrada, Bill Payne and Richie Hayward, who came from George's band the Factory; the classic sextet by late 1972 (Kenny Gradney, Paul Barrere, Sam Clayton). Broke up in 1979 after George's death, re-formed in 1987. Hayward: drums, backing vocals, 1969-1979 and 1987-2010; a motorcycle accident before The Last Record Album (1975); liver disease announced August 2009, Gabe Ford in his place; died 12 August 2010. Hayward joined Ike Turner when the band disbanded in late 1973; drummer on Robert Plant's Shaken 'n' Stirred (1985).

title: Richie Hayward: The MD Interviews, Part 1 (Modern Drummer, March 1988; posted October 2010)
notes: Robyn Flans. Ames, Iowa; a Montgomery Ward kit at eleven; Jack Sperling his first hero; never a double bass player, "I do exchanges between the left hand and the right foot instead of between two feet"; answered "Drummer wanted. Must be freaky" (Lowell George, the Factory, 1966); Lowell wanted him "to stay more in the groove", so he filled with the left hand and right foot while keeping the hat going; the Meters, Clifton Chenier and Professor Longhair; fired in '74 and called back for Feats Don't Fail Me Now; "Fat Man" jammed for three years before it was recorded; Cold, Cold, Cold's drums overdubbed on Lowell George's drum machine; in traction from a motorcycle accident when George died in 1979; Simmons pads with Robert Plant; "real American with second-line and jazz overtones"; "Listen to Ziggy [Modeliste]. He's one of my all-time heroes."

title: Richie Hayward: The MD Interviews, Part 2 (Modern Drummer cover story, October 1995; posted November 2010)
notes: Robyn Flans. Influences: Sonny Payne first, the blues drummers behind Muddy Waters and Howlin' Wolf, Tony Williams, Elvin Jones, Max Roach, Art Blakey; Zig Modeliste, Jim Keltner and Jeff Porcaro; Mitch Mitchell for going out with the soloist. Fills between the left hand and right foot "because Lowell kept telling me not to do fills"; paradiddles between the left hand and right foot; the bass drum "as a tom". Clamps his cymbals, sits low (Porcaro's influence), "fourteen or fifteen snare drums" for a Little Feat session, a second hi-hat for Hate to Lose Your Lovin', splashes, a pre-war Radio King for acoustic shows. Three tracks that are him: The Fan, Rock and Roll Doctor or Fat Man in the Bathtub; Fat Man "one of my first experiments in second line ... it changes feel about six times"; Mercenary Territory's solo in 10/4.

title: Waiting for Columbus - Wikipedia
notes: Little Feat's first live album, Warner Bros., 10 February 1978: the Rainbow Theatre, London, 1-4 August 1977, and the Lisner Auditorium, Washington, 8-10 August 1977, with the Tower of Power horns. Fat Man in the Bathtub 4:50, Mercenary Territory 4:27; Richard Hayward, drums, vocals.

title: The Last Record Album - Wikipedia
notes: 1975. The sleeve was decorated with Hayward's hospital bills after a serious motorcycle accident (Adam Sweeting, The Guardian, 2010).

title: Little Feat - Feats Don't Fail Me Now (Warner Bros. BS 2784, 1974), credits on Discogs
notes: The sleeve credits: Richie Hayward, drums and background vocals; Sam Clayton, percussion; no other drummer, and no Fred White or Gordon DeWitty. The 2016 reissue (R1 2784, release 8708474) and the 2024 deluxe edition (release 30966925, with per-track engineer and producer credits) name Hayward as the only drummer as well.
